Chain, middleware, security, async-stream, context, and stability claims are scoped explicitly.

evidence: Checked handler outcome algebra, least non-pass index, completeness quantification, eligibility/overlap/gap notation, visited prefix, sequential cost, and immutable configuration-generation model.

Confirmed 2048 exceeds 1024 and rejects after size only.
Confirmed missing small request visits all three and terminates at not-found.
Recomputed exercise selections and reproduced all three exact output lines.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Visit counts and comparisons cover finite sequential inputs only, not production distributions or concurrent behavior.

evidence: Traced Pass versus terminal dispositions for all executable branches.
Enumerated q1/q2 overlap on negative evens and q3 overlap with every value; verified swapping first two changes -2 selection.
Checked total fallback closes gaps for inputs reaching it.
Checked generation publication preserves one immutable chain per in-flight request.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Totality applies only to the demonstrated fallback function and declared input form, not unknown deployed configurations.

evidence: Reviewed zero/one/many handlers, gaps, overlaps, duplicate/cyclic/ambiguous order, early terminal, pass-after-mutation, failure-then-fallback, missing policy, cache/static security bypass, and terminal outcome modeling.

Reviewed concurrent singleton state, reentrancy, async double/late continuation, cancellation/deadline, live reconfiguration, handler close, stream demand/signals, unbounded plugin cost/telemetry, indeterminate actuation, and independent safety controls.

evidence: Checked explicit dispositions, deterministic inspectable order, exact visited prefix, mandatory security, context propagation, state isolation, distinct failure outcomes, and bounded chain/resource/telemetry behavior against exposition and answers.

evidence: Reviewed the three finite dispatch traces and predicate-selection derivation line by line.
Reviewed completeness and mandatory-mediation arguments with their finite-domain/total-fallback/complete-graph assumptions.

evidence: Audited exactly, total, complete, deterministic, immutable, safe, atomic, guarantee, prove, must, and conclusion language.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Coverage and safety claims retain stated domains/mechanisms; future security and high-stakes evidence is not presented as complete.

evidence: Reproduced deterministic handling, rejection, fallback, and visited-handler outputs.
Dynamic configuration, concurrency, async/stream, route-security, fault/load, hardware, and safety evidence remains prescribed future work.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production completeness, security, performance, external academic/practitioner review, or system safety is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter defines Chain of Responsibility through explicit dispositions and least-index selection, integrating completeness, order, pass effects, security, context, failure, async/stream behavior, concurrency/lifecycle, observability, testing, and simplification.

practitioner_review.notes: Guidance covers stable descriptors, before/after constraints, immutable generation rollout, side-effect-light pass, authorization coverage, remaining deadlines, exactly-once continuation, bounded backpressure/telemetry, configuration digests, canaries, and rollback.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review begins with a formal first-match model, supplies a runnable three-outcome chain, broadens through ten distinct cases, and includes five complete exercises spanning tracing, predicate algebra, registry design, async security, and high-stakes transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
